title: Foundations of AI Ethics
description: An introductory workshop exploring the fundamental ethical considerations in artificial intelligence development and deployment. Participants engage in hands-on activities to understand bias, fairness, and transparency in AI systems.
learningObjectives: Understand core ethical principles applicable to AI systems
Identify potential sources of bias in AI development
Recognize the importance of transparency and explainability
Apply ethical frameworks to real-world AI scenarios

activities.title: AI in Our Lives
activities.description: Participants share personal experiences with AI systems and discuss their ethical concerns

activities.title: Core Ethical Principles
activities.description: Introduction to key ethical frameworks: beneficence, non-maleficence, autonomy, justice, and explicability

activities.title: Real-World Ethics Cases
activities.description: Group discussion on recent AI ethics controversies in the news

activities.title: Bias Detection Exercise
activities.description: Hands-on activity using a simulated dataset to identify and measure bias in machine learning models

activities.title: Fairness Metrics Workshop
activities.description: Teams work to define fairness metrics for different AI application scenarios

activities.title: Mitigation Strategies
activities.description: Overview of techniques to reduce bias in AI systems

activities.title: Black Box vs. Explainable AI
activities.description: Analysis of trade-offs between model performance and interpretability

activities.title: Explainability Tools
activities.description: Practical introduction to SHAP and LIME for model explanation

activities.title: Accountability Frameworks
activities.description: Brief overview of governance and accountability structures

activities.title: Personal Ethics Statement
activities.description: Participants draft their personal AI ethics principles

activities.title: Commitments and Next Steps
activities.description: Sharing of key takeaways and action commitments

prerequisites: Basic understanding of machine learning concepts
facilitatorNotes: This workshop works best with a mix of technical and non-technical participants. Ensure hands-on activities are accessible to those with limited coding experience by providing pre-written code templates.

title: Effective Human-AI Collaboration
description: A comprehensive workshop on designing and implementing effective human-AI collaborative systems. Participants explore interaction patterns, trust dynamics, and best practices for augmenting human capabilities with AI.
learningObjectives: Understand different models of human-AI collaboration
Design AI systems that complement human strengths
Build trust and transparency in AI partnerships
Evaluate and improve human-AI team performance

activities.title: Collaboration Spectrum
activities.description: Overview of collaboration models from full automation to AI-assisted decision-making

activities.title: Mapping Collaboration Patterns
activities.description: Teams analyze real-world systems and map them to collaboration models

activities.title: When to Automate vs. Augment
activities.description: Group discussion on decision criteria for automation levels

activities.title: Task Analysis Exercise
activities.description: Breaking down tasks to identify human vs. AI comparative advantages

activities.title: Interface Design Sprint
activities.description: Rapid prototyping of human-AI interfaces using design thinking principles

activities.title: Design Showcase
activities.description: Teams present and review each other's interface designs

activities.title: Trust Scenarios
activities.description: Simulated scenarios exploring trust calibration, over-reliance, and appropriate skepticism

activities.title: Trust Factors in AI
activities.description: Research-backed insights on transparency, reliability, and user control

activities.title: Transparency Dashboard Design
activities.description: Creating transparency features that build appropriate trust

activities.title: Human-AI Team Metrics
activities.description: Demonstration of metrics beyond accuracy: user satisfaction, time savings, learning effects

activities.title: Collaborative Task Simulation
activities.description: Participants work with AI tools on realistic tasks and measure outcomes
tools: Custom simulation platform or case-based exercises

activities.title: Lessons Learned
activities.description: Debriefing on collaboration experiences and improvement opportunities

prerequisites: Experience with product design or UX helpful but not required
facilitatorNotes: The role-play and simulation activities are crucial for experiential learning. Ensure adequate time for debriefing to extract key insights. Mix teams to combine technical and domain expertise.

title: AI Governance in Practice
description: A practical workshop on implementing AI governance frameworks within organizations. Participants work through real-world scenarios to establish policies, processes, and oversight mechanisms for responsible AI.
learningObjectives: Understand key components of AI governance frameworks
Develop practical policies for AI development and deployment
Design review processes for AI systems
Create accountability structures for AI projects

activities.title: Governance Frameworks Overview
activities.description: Introduction to major AI governance frameworks: EU AI Act, NIST AI RMF, IEEE standards

activities.title: Stakeholder Mapping
activities.description: Identifying stakeholders and their governance concerns in AI projects

activities.title: Governance Challenges
activities.description: Open discussion on common organizational challenges

activities.title: Policy Gap Analysis
activities.description: Analyzing an organization's existing policies for AI readiness

activities.title: Policy Drafting Exercise
activities.description: Teams draft AI use policies for specific scenarios (hiring, lending, healthcare, etc.)

activities.title: Policy Review Session
activities.description: Teams exchange and critique each other's draft policies

activities.title: AI Impact Assessments
activities.description: Introduction to algorithmic impact assessments and risk evaluation

activities.title: Risk Assessment Exercise
activities.description: Conducting a simplified AI impact assessment for a realistic scenario

activities.title: Review Board Simulation
activities.description: Role-playing an AI ethics review board meeting

activities.title: Governance Roadmap
activities.description: Creating an implementation plan for AI governance in participants' organizations

activities.title: Commitments and Resources
activities.description: Group sharing of plans and resource recommendations

prerequisites: Familiarity with organizational policy development helpful
facilitatorNotes: Tailor scenarios to participants' industries when possible. The policy drafting exercise benefits from diverse team composition. Have legal/compliance expertise available for questions.

title: AI and Social Impact: Navigating Challenges
description: An engaging workshop examining the broader societal implications of AI technology. Participants explore issues of equity, employment, privacy, and democratic participation through interactive discussions and scenario planning.
learningObjectives: Analyze AI's impact on employment and economic equity
Understand privacy implications of AI systems
Explore AI's role in democratic processes and civic engagement
Develop strategies for equitable AI deployment

activities.title: AI, Automation, and Work
activities.description: Overview of AI's impact on employment, job transformation, and inequality

activities.title: Future of Work Debate
activities.description: Structured debate on AI's role in job displacement vs. job creation

activities.title: Inclusive AI Design
activities.description: Teams design AI applications that promote economic inclusion

activities.title: Data Collection Revelation
activities.description: Eye-opening demonstration of how much data AI systems collect and infer

activities.title: Privacy-Preserving Design
activities.description: Hands-on exploration of privacy-preserving techniques: differential privacy, federated learning

activities.title: Privacy vs. Utility Trade-offs
activities.description: Group discussion on balancing privacy protection with AI capabilities

activities.title: AI in Public Decision-Making
activities.description: Analysis of AI use in government services, criminal justice, and civic processes

activities.title: Algorithmic Governance Simulation
activities.description: Participants role-play stakeholders in a public AI deployment decision

activities.title: Democratic AI Principles
activities.description: Synthesis of key principles for democratic AI governance

activities.title: Stakeholder Action Plans
activities.description: Developing concrete actions for different stakeholder groups (developers, policymakers, citizens)

activities.title: Commitments and Resources
activities.description: Sharing commitments and distributing advocacy resources

facilitatorNotes: This workshop benefits from diverse participant backgrounds. Encourage respectful dialogue during debates and discussions. Be prepared to moderate sensitive topics around employment and inequality.

title: Responsible AI Development Lifecycle
description: A hands-on technical workshop for AI practitioners on integrating ethical considerations throughout the AI development lifecycle. Participants work through the complete process from problem framing to deployment and monitoring.
learningObjectives: Apply ethical frameworks at each stage of AI development
Implement fairness and bias testing in ML pipelines
Design monitoring systems for deployed AI
Create documentation for responsible AI systems

activities.title: Beyond the Technical: Problem Framing
activities.description: How problem definition shapes ethical outcomes in AI projects

activities.title: Stakeholder Impact Analysis
activities.description: Using structured templates to analyze stakeholder impacts for an AI project

activities.title: Problem Reframing Exercise
activities.description: Teams reframe problematic AI project definitions to align with ethical principles

activities.title: Data Ethics Principles
activities.description: Consent, minimization, quality, and representativeness in data collection

activities.title: Bias Audit in Datasets
activities.description: Using Python tools to detect and analyze bias in training datasets

activities.title: Data Documentation
activities.description: Creating datasheets for datasets following best practices

activities.title: Fairness Metrics and Trade-offs
activities.description: Overview of fairness definitions and impossibility results

activities.title: Fairness-Aware Training
activities.description: Implementing bias mitigation techniques in model training

activities.title: Model Explainability
activities.description: Generating explanations for model predictions using SHAP and LIME

activities.title: Responsible Deployment Practices
activities.description: Staged rollouts, human-in-the-loop systems, and monitoring strategies

activities.title: Monitoring Dashboard Setup
activities.description: Building dashboards to track fairness metrics and model drift in production

activities.title: Model Cards Creation
activities.description: Documenting models using the model cards framework

prerequisites: Familiarity with scikit-learn or similar ML libraries
materials: Laptops with Python environment (Jupyter, required libraries)
Access to cloud computing resources (optional but helpful)
facilitatorNotes: This is a technical workshop requiring hands-on coding. Ensure all participants have working Python environments before starting. Provide code solutions for those who struggle. Consider using cloud notebooks (Google Colab, Kaggle) to minimize setup issues.

title: Cross-Cultural Perspectives on AI Ethics
description: An exploratory workshop examining how cultural contexts shape AI ethics. Participants engage with diverse ethical frameworks and learn to design AI systems that respect cultural differences and promote global justice.
learningObjectives: Understand how cultural values influence AI ethics
Recognize Western bias in dominant AI ethics frameworks
Design culturally sensitive AI applications
Apply principles of global justice to AI development

activities.title: Ethics Across Cultures
activities.description: Comparing ethical frameworks: Western individualism, Ubuntu philosophy, Confucian ethics, Islamic principles

activities.title: Cultural Values Exercise
activities.description: Small groups discuss how cultural values shape AI ethics priorities (privacy, community, authority, etc.)

activities.title: Cross-Cultural Insights
activities.description: Groups share insights and identify common ground and differences

activities.title: Global AI Failures
activities.description: Analysis of AI systems that failed due to cultural insensitivity or bias

activities.title: Language and Cultural Bias
activities.description: Hands-on exploration of bias in NLP models across languages and cultures

activities.title: Data Colonialism
activities.description: Critical discussion on data extraction and AI imperialism

activities.title: Inclusive Design Principles
activities.description: Best practices for culturally responsive AI development

activities.title: Cultural Adaptation Challenge
activities.description: Teams redesign an AI application for specific cultural contexts

activities.title: Design Review
activities.description: Teams present adaptations and provide peer feedback

prerequisites: Basic understanding of AI ethics concepts
Openness to diverse perspectives and respectful dialogue
facilitatorNotes: Ensure facilitators have cultural competence and can navigate sensitive discussions. Include participants from diverse backgrounds when possible. Acknowledge power dynamics in the room and create safe space for all voices.
